The ENCOMB project (Extended Non-Destructive Testing of Composite Bonds) was an FP7 EU project that screened NDT methods for bonded aerospace composite structures.
Current aerospace certification rules prohibit certification of aircraft composite structures with solely bonded joints without additional rivets for safety.
The ComBoNDT project is a Horizon 2020 EU project that continued research from ENCOMB, focusing on the most promising ENDT methods.
EMI measurements were performed using an IM3570 laboratory impedance analyzer (Hioki) with focus on conductance spectra up to 5 MHz.
The piezoelectric disc transducer used in EMI experiments had a 10 mm diameter and 0.5 mm thickness, manufactured by CeramTec (SONOXP502 material).
For flat coupon EMI samples in the production scenario, a local resonance was identified in the 4.3-4.7 MHz bandwidth.
The relative frequency shift between reference EMI samples was only -0.027%, establishing a baseline threshold for contamination detection.
In EMI repair scenario experiments, thermal degradation at higher temperatures resulted in increased frequency shifts.
For curved pilot samples in EMI testing, only 3 out of 6 contaminated samples exceeded the reference threshold of 1.71% frequency shift.
LASAT uses a high-power Nd-YAG laser with energy between 1-40 J and pulse durations of 3-20 ns.
Laser shock pressures generated in LASAT range from 1-5 GPa, with power density of 1-10 GW/cm².
Water confinement in LASAT can multiply generated stresses by up to four times for the same laser intensity.
The symmetrical LASAT configuration creates a primary tensile stress area and a secondary area where reflected shock waves cross.
Aluminum sacrificial tape is applied to sample surfaces in LASAT to prevent laser ablation and ensure repeatability.
Ultrasound scanning is required after LASAT to detect defects created by laser shock, with specific signatures for front face, bond, and back echo.
In LASAT experiments, 20 shots were performed at each of 11 different laser intensities ranging from 5 to 100% of maximum intensity.
The standard deviation in LASAT shot reproducibility was less than 1% across all intensity levels.
Diffractive Optical Elements (DOE) are used in the Hephaistos facility to smooth focal spots and create homogeneous pressure distribution.
The GAÏA laser at Hephaistos consists of two different lasers with beams polarized 90° from each other.
NUS revealed increased nonlinearity at the CFRP-adhesive interphase for single contamination scenarios on flat and scarfed samples.
Multiple contaminations on curved samples showed decreased nonlinearity in NUS measurements.
The research investigated both single contamination and combined contamination scenarios across different sample geometries.
Sample geometries tested included flat coupon samples, curved pilot samples, and scarfed bonding samples.
Production-related contamination scenarios included release agent, moisture, and fingerprint (artificial sweat) contamination.
Repair-related contamination scenarios included thermal degradation, de-icer contamination, and faulty adhesive curing.
Some EMI measurement results were rejected due to different spectrum shapes, indicating sensitivity to sample preparation and bonding quality.
The research demonstrated that ENDT methods could potentially identify not-in-order (NIO) joints during bondline assessment.
Components of real aerospace structures with stringers were investigated in the ComBoNDT project, with findings reported in subsequent chapters.
The paper emphasizes that adhesive bonding enables weight reduction through elimination or reduction of riveted joints compared to aluminum-based structures.
"Chicken rivets" is the aerospace term for rivets used in conjunction with adhesive bondlines to ensure reliability in case of bondline failure.
